tldr: Eleven source-linked reports cover November 9 AI developments in model compression, computing power, business and regulation, alongside three explicitly dated November 5–6 catch-up research releases.
The seven Reuters-reported developments remain attributed reporting, and first-party research benchmarks are not independently reproduced; source coverage is partial.
Three technology and three terminology proposals remain deferred for catalog checks, with zero canonical IDs added.

news.title: Amazon details HOPE pruning that preserves cooperating MoE experts
news.summary: Amazon's November 9 technical walkthrough describes its open-source HOPE implementation, which chooses experts to prune using pairwise interactions rather than independent importance ranks. The research paper itself was first posted September 16.
news.why_it_matters: Aggressive MoE compression may better retain long-horizon coding behavior when co-activated experts are pruned together carefully.
news.caveat: Up-to-6.1% agentic-coding gains are author-reported on selected models and benchmarks; no independent replication; smaller pruning fractions may offer less benefit.

news.title: Norway pauses new data-center grid reservations pending licensing
news.summary: Reuters reports that Norway's grid operator Statnett paused new data-center connection reservations while a licensing scheme prioritizing essential infrastructure is developed.
news.why_it_matters: Grid capacity and approvals can constrain where AI clusters are built as much as hardware availability.
news.caveat: A pause on new reservations is not a shutdown of existing centers; 26,000 MW in reported grid requests is not realized electricity demand.

news.title: AI developers look to used turbines and retired jet engines for electricity
news.summary: Reuters interviews equipment suppliers and analysts who describe AI data-center developers sourcing refurbished turbines and converted aircraft engines amid multiyear new-equipment backlogs.
news.why_it_matters: Energy infrastructure supply chains may determine practical AI compute expansion.
news.caveat: Capacity and delivery-time estimates are attributed to industry analysts, while used-equipment reliability and permitting remain unresolved.

news.title: US president signals conditional openness to AI guardrails
news.summary: In a November 8 television interview reported by Reuters on November 9 UTC, President Trump described AI risks as manageable and said he would consider some safeguards.
news.why_it_matters: Signals possible policy positioning as lawmakers debate AI rules.
news.caveat: Remarks are not legislation, a formal regulatory proposal, or a confirmed bipartisan agreement.

news.title: Disney and Adobe agree to develop private creative AI models
news.summary: Reuters reports a multi-year Disney–Adobe agreement to develop Disney-specific generative models through Firefly Foundry for concept development and other media uses.
news.why_it_matters: Illustrates enterprise demand for IP-specific model customization rather than generic public generation tools.
news.caveat: Workflow acceleration is attributed to participating companies; resulting models are proprietary and not independently benchmarked.

news.title: Apple Intelligence gets regulatory registration for laptops and tablets in China
news.summary: Reuters reports that Shanghai's cyberspace regulator has registered Apple Intelligence for use on tablets and laptops, following earlier iPhone approval.
news.why_it_matters: Market-specific regulation and local model partnerships affect the actual rollout of consumer AI.
news.caveat: Registration does not establish that services are already live on all devices; rollout details are separately attributed.

news.title: US safety regulator opens follow-up query on Waymo school-bus behavior
news.summary: Reuters reports that NHTSA opened a recall query covering 2,895 Waymo vehicles to assess a prior software remedy involving stopped school buses.
news.why_it_matters: Deployed autonomous-system fixes require evidence of effectiveness after release.
news.caveat: An opened regulatory inquiry is not a determination that the remedy failed or that every listed vehicle committed a violation.

news.title: Taiwan reports October export record amid demand for AI hardware
news.summary: Taiwan's finance ministry reported October exports up 58.9% year on year to $96.76 billion, with electronic components up 61.4%, according to Reuters on November 9.
news.why_it_matters: A quantifiable signal of hardware supply-chain expansion amid AI and broader technology demand.
news.caveat: October trade figures are not November sales and include non-AI products; correlation with AI investment is not a precise AI-revenue measure.

news.title: LingYu shares 139-hour first-person dual-arm robot demonstration dataset
news.summary: LingYu Robotics reports 139.4 hours of synchronized first-person videos, state signals and teleoperation commands across 13,263 successful episodes from 22 tabletop subsets.
news.why_it_matters: Offers robot-view demonstration data aligned with action outputs for embodied policy research.
news.caveat: Success-only episodes omit failures and recovery; the public dataset is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and restricted to noncommercial uses.

news.title: Sand3D publishes 106,094 objects as short procedural Python programs
news.summary: Sandflow describes a Python/Blender 3D modeling library and a dataset of 106,094 objects represented as construction programs, including 10,456 articulated examples.
news.why_it_matters: A consistent code representation could support editable 3D generation by language models.
news.caveat: Mainly hard-surface assets, no verified real-world robotics accuracy; source-object license obligations remain despite the dataset umbrella.

news.title: Weather-model study tests FP16 compute with FP32 physical state
news.summary: A November 6 arXiv preprint tests five weather-prediction networks, reporting 1.3–3.5x faster ten-day forecasts when model layers use FP16 but physical state and conversions stay FP32.
news.why_it_matters: Separating network arithmetic precision from numerical state can reduce inference costs in weather applications.
news.caveat: Author-reported study uses 52 initialization dates and one 16 GB GPU; performance and error bounds are not general guarantees or peer-reviewed replication.
